reversed.libraryEntry: Three reversals and none of them involves losing anything. The first is non-occupancy. The corner is finished, functioning, and unvisited, because you moved straight to the next unbuilt thing, and a finished corner has no mechanism for requesting attention. Ease does not announce itself and cannot compete with an unfinished project for anybody's evening. The second is quiet decay. Established is a state with a shelf life, and the maintenance window is much less visible than the building was, so fences go soft while being described as done. The third is the uncomfortable one. Sufficiency and settling produce the same latched gate, and the distinction is entirely internal. Nobody on the road can tell, no test resolves it, and whether this is enough or merely what got accepted is one of those questions that only becomes answerable when asked directly, alone, with nobody to perform contentment for.

meanings.altText: Nine round Lunaria seed pods in four rows of two with one centered between them.

readingLines: The trees in that garden were planted by somebody dead before you were born. Ten pods, ranked. None of them the first. You are eating from work you did not do, and something you are doing now works the same way.
Ten pods on one stem, and the stem is not the point. Continuity is. Somebody kept a house, a recipe, a set of tools, a fruit tree, and you are standing in the result. Nobody asked you for anything.

Ten pods, generations of them. Some wealth is measured in whether the thing outlasts your interest in it, and most of what you inherited was made by people who never saw it working. You are mid-chain, not at either end.
questions: Whose work are you standing in?
What are you keeping for somebody later?
Who planted the thing you use daily?
meanings.libraryEntry: Ten pods ranked on a plate, and the point of the arrangement is that no single one of them is the original. The ten is the suit's longest view. Lunaria self-seeds, comes back in beds nobody has tended for years, and turns up in gardens whose planters are long gone, which makes it the right plant for a card about continuity. Most of what holds your life up was built by people who never saw it working. A house, a recipe, a rule about Sundays, a fruit tree, a habit of showing up. None of it was ever paid for and none of it can be repaid to the people who did it, which leaves only the option of continuing it. That is the quiet proposal here. You are in the middle of a chain rather than at either end of it, and the middle has obligations that arrive without paperwork.

readingLines: You planted something you may not see finish. A tree, a fund, a practice, a child's competence. Ten pods and none of them the last either. That is the only immortality this deck offers. That is enough of a claim.

You are living on the inheritance and adding nothing to it. Ten pods, all from earlier hands. Coasting on continuity works for a long time and then stops, usually without notice, in somebody else's generation.
The inheritance came with terms. A house with a mortgage of expectations, a trade you did not choose, a name to keep up, and ten pods you were handed rather than grew. Some of it can be put down.
questions: What did you plant for later?
What have you added to it?
Which inherited term could you set down?
reversed.libraryEntry: Three positions in the chain, and all of them are ordinary. The first is planting. You put something in that you may not see finish, a tree, a practice, a child's competence, and the deck offers no other version of continuing past yourself. The second is coasting. Living on what earlier hands built while adding nothing to it works for a surprisingly long time, because well-built things carry passengers, and then it stops, usually without notice and usually in somebody else's generation rather than yours. The third is the inheritance that arrived with terms. A house that came with expectations, a trade nobody chose, a name to keep up, ten pods handed over rather than grown. Some of those terms are worth keeping and some were never yours to accept, and the distinction is available to be made rather than simply lived with.

meanings.altText: Ten round Lunaria seed pods in four rows of two with two centered between them.

readingLines: One page a day, filled by you, for eleven weeks. A sprout above one pod. Diligence is curiosity that shows up on schedule, and the schedule is doing more work than the curiosity is. Both are needed. Only one is reliable.

You have kept a small thing going for longer than you have noticed. A page, a stretch, ten minutes, some unremarkable daily item. Nobody has praised it because there is nothing yet to praise. There is however a stack.
A sprout above a seed pod, both drawn plainly. Like the page of this suit, you study. The pace is that of somebody who intends to still be here in a year. Slow is the strategy. Not the limitation.
questions: What have you kept going without noticing?
How many days is it now?
Who else knows you do it?
meanings.libraryEntry: Diligence has a bad name because it photographs badly. The notebook with one page filled every day for eleven weeks produces nothing worth showing at week eleven, and it is the reason somebody is competent at week two hundred. Lunaria takes a season and gives no weekly report, and this is the youngest card in the suit that already understands that. What makes the page unusual is that the schedule is carrying the curiosity rather than the reverse. Interest is unreliable and turns up when it likes. A daily slot turns up whether or not interest does, and the slot is what accumulates. There is no drama available here and none required. You, keeping a small ordinary thing going, unpraised because there is not yet anything to praise, quietly building the one asset that compounds without supervision. Nobody supervises it, which is exactly why it holds.

readingLines: The streak broke on a Thursday. You started again on the Friday. That is the actual skill, and it is not the streak. Nobody who keeps anything for years has an unbroken record of it.

Your streak became the point. Eleven weeks of pages, and the pages have stopped containing anything. The requirement is now the mark on the calendar, not the ten minutes it was meant to protect. The ticks are immaculate. The pages are empty.
You are studying instead of doing. A page a day about the thing, for eleven weeks, and no version of the thing itself yet. Preparation is genuinely pleasant and it is not the same as the work.
questions: When did you start again?
What is on the pages lately?
Studying, or doing?
reversed.libraryEntry: Three failures of the daily habit, and the first is not a failure at all. A streak breaks on a Thursday and gets restarted on the Friday, and the restarting is the skill rather than the streak, because nobody who has kept anything for years has an unbroken record of it. The people who look consistent are the people who resumed quickly. The second is the calendar mark becoming the requirement. Eleven weeks of pages that no longer contain anything, kept because the row of ticks now has to be defended, and the ten minutes your habit existed to protect have quietly been evicted by the habit. The third is study as a substitute. A page a day about the work, faithfully, and no version of the work. Preparation is pleasant, visible, and available in unlimited quantities to anyone avoiding a first attempt.

meanings.altText: A small sprout sigil above one round Lunaria pod, moss mark above.

readingLines: You hoed the whole row, including the middle, where nobody was watching and nothing was interesting. A chevron above one pod. Thoroughness is unglamorous until it turns out to be the entire difference. Nobody is standing at the middle of a row.

The middle of the row is where most rows get abandoned. Not the start, which is exciting, and not the end, which is visible. The middle, which is neither. You have been in a middle lately and you are still hoeing.

A chevron above a seed pod. Both plain, neither hurried. Like the knight of this suit, you are the slowest thing in the court and the one that finishes. Reliability looks unremarkable from outside. From inside it looks like a finished row.
questions: Which middle are you in?
What did you finish that nobody saw?
Who relies on you for this?
meanings.libraryEntry: The middle of the row is where things get abandoned. Beginnings recruit attention and endings are visible from a distance, and between them is a stretch that is neither, in which the work is identical and the interest is gone. Getting through that stretch is the entire competence this card describes. Lunaria's knight is the slowest figure in the deck's court and the one that arrives, and those two facts are the same fact. What makes the middle hard is not difficulty. It is the absence of feedback in either direction, no novelty and no finish line, just the same motion in a part of the field nobody visits. Whoever depends on you probably depends on this rather than on anything you would list. Yours is invisible until the one occasion it is the whole difference. That occasion arrives without notice.

readingLines: You finished the row. Nobody mentioned it. That is standard, and not a slight. Finished rows do not announce themselves, and the person who notices them is usually the one who hoed. You noticed. That is the usual arrangement.

The row stopped two thirds along. Not from laziness, from the middle, which is where rows stop. You could pick it up where it stopped. That point is closer to the end than the abandoning made it feel.

You are hoeing a row nobody needs finished. Thoroughness with no judgement attached hoes anything, including a field planted by mistake, and does it beautifully, all season. Diligence has no opinion about direction. Nobody checks the direction of a good worker.
questions: What did you finish unremarked?
Where did the row stop?
Which row does not need finishing?
reversed.libraryEntry: Three ways thoroughness plays out. The first is the unremarked finish. A row gets completed, nobody mentions it, and that is the standard result rather than a slight, because finished rows are silent by nature and the only reliable witness is the person who hoed. The second is the two-thirds stop, which happens in the middle and not from laziness, and it leaves the work closer to done than the abandoning made it feel. Picking up where it stopped is generally a smaller job than starting anything. The third is the harder one. Thoroughness carries no opinion about direction, so it hoes whatever row it is pointed at, including a field planted by mistake, and it does that beautifully for an entire season. Diligence is a wonderful engine and a poor navigator, and it very rarely asks you whether the row was the right one.

meanings.altText: A double chevron above one round Lunaria pod, moss mark above.

readingLines: Provision, warm and practical — the kind that arrives before it's asked for. Care, in this suit, looks like handled logistics.
questions: Who do you take care of by handling things, and do they know?

readingLines: Harvest in the barn, stewardship in the posture. Security kept in trust rather than in a fist.
questions: What resource of yours does the most good when shared?
